Posterior hindcasts for an mvgam state-space model

Source: R/hindcast.mvgam.R
hindcast.mvgam.Rd

Posterior draws at the training time points. Each draw takes the latent state the model inferred at each time. The observation family maps it to the response scale. A hindcast shows how closely the fitted states track the data. forecast.mvgam() predicts unseen times.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'mvgam'
hindcast(
  object,
  ...,
  type = c("response", "link", "expected", "trend", "latent_state"),
  component = NULL,
  ndraws = NULL,
  draw_ids = NULL,
  obs_uncertainty = TRUE,
  process_error = FALSE,
  resp = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted mvgam object.

...

Unused. Anything passed here is refused.

type

The scale of the draws, as in forecast.mvgam(), or "latent_state" for a closure-unit family. "latent_state" returns the occupancy probability psi of an occ() model or the abundance N of an nmix() model at each closure unit, as an mvgam_latent_state object with print(), summary(), as.data.frame() and plot() methods.

component

NULL (the default) for the summed trend, or the names of state components of the trend, with type = "trend". Several names give the sum of their components. LLT() has "level", the stochastic level, and "slope", its growth per time step. A seasonal LLT() adds "season". "predictor" holds the effects of the trend formula's covariates. c("level", "predictor") gives the level with those effects. A factor model projects each component through its loadings, as it projects the trend. The result is an ordinary mvgam_forecast-class with the components in its component slot.

ndraws

Positive integer specifying number of posterior draws to use. NULL (default) uses all available draws.

draw_ids

Optional integer vector selecting a subset of posterior draw indices to use. NULL (default) uses all draws (subject to ndraws).

obs_uncertainty

Logical. When FALSE, skips observation-family sampling for type = "response", returning the family mean instead. Defaults to TRUE.

process_error

Logical. FALSE (the default) takes the fitted latent state of each draw. type = "response" then adds the observation noise alone. TRUE adds fresh trend innovations to the linear predictor, as posterior_epred.mvgam() does with the same argument. A component is a fitted state and needs FALSE.

resp

Character specifying which response variable for multivariate models. NULL (default) returns predictions for all responses.

Value

An mvgam_forecast-class object. Its hindcasts are a named list of [ndraws, n_times] matrices, one per series. Its forecast slots are NULL.

See also

forecast.mvgam() extrapolates the fitted state. posterior_predict.mvgam() and posterior_epred.mvgam() predict by integrating over the trend's dynamics. The multivariate article compares type = "trend" hindcasts of one latent state from a joint model and from each data source alone. The N-mixture article summarises type = "latent_state" hindcasts of abundance.

Other predictions: conditional_effects.mvgam(), conditional_smooths.mvgam(), fitted.mvgam(), posterior_epred.mvgam(), posterior_linpred.mvgam(), posterior_predict.mvgam(), posterior_smooths.mvgam(), predict.mvgam(), predictive_error.mvgam(), predictive_interval.mvgam()

Other forecasting: compare_scores(), ensemble.mvgam_forecast(), forecast.mvgam(), lfo_cv.mvgam(), score.mvgam_forecast()

Examples

# \dontrun{
set.seed(11)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 1L,
                     n_timepoints = 120L, trend_model = AR())

mod <- mvgam(
  y ~ s(x),
  trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1),
  data    = simdat$data_train,
  family  = poisson(),
  chains  = 2, silent = 2
)
#> Warning: 386 of 2000 (19.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.

# The fitted states track the training counts
hc <- hindcast(mod)
plot(hc)


# The AR(1) trend on the log scale
plot(hindcast(mod, type = "trend"))


# Fresh innovations in place of the fitted states give the wider
# spread a model without the observed history would predict
plot(hindcast(mod, process_error = TRUE))


# A local linear trend's slope, the level's growth per step
mod_llt <- update(mod, trend_formula = ~ LLT())
#> Warning: 3 of 2000 (0.0%) transitions ended with a divergence.
#> See https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings for details.
plot(hindcast(mod_llt, type = "trend", component = "slope"))


# Next, forecast the held-out times with forecast()
# }
